newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- South Africa's credit binge continued in October with figures released on Friday showing that Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals was compelled to act to curb demand or risk an upsurge in inflation.
- The continued rise in oil prices this year has cost South African oil companies about 500 million rand in lost revenue.
- The ruling African National Congress nominated South African Broadcasting Corporation board chairman Ivy Matsepe-Casaburri as Free State premier.

- MIH Holdings Ltd reported a sharp increase in attributable loss to 122.1 million rand in the six months to September on the back of continued costs related to development of pay television operations in African and Europe.

- South Africa's building and construction industry will get a boost from the Reconstruction and Development Programme next year with activity in the sector rising between eight and nine percent, the Building Research Strategy Consulting Unit said.
- Nasionale Pers Beperk (Naspers) lifted net earnings before extraordinary items, by 25 percent to 48 million rand for the six months to September 30.
- The long-awaited tie-up between Times Media Limited and British media group Pearson Plc might be delayed by a Appeal Court judgment in favour of printing and publishing group Caxton Ltd.
- The girlfriend of Ferdi Barnard, a former Civil Cooperation Bureau operative, has turned state witness and blown the lid on police killings and high level corruption.
